syllabus.quote: Evaluate judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something

one_line: Give points for AND against. Add a consequence to each point and say how much it matters in this scenario. End with a reasoned overall judgement.

points.text: You must write about both sides. Some 2022-2023 mark schemes cap answers that are all for or all against at 6 of 8. This is 3 of the 24 Evaluate mark schemes from 2022 on. Two mark schemes say you need at least two points on each side for full marks.

cites.quote: Max 6 if all for or all against. Max 6 marks if bullets/list of points.
Must be at least two of each for full marks. Max 6 marks if bullets/list of points.
Must be at least 2 strengths and at least 2 weaknesses for full marks.

points.text: Recent mark schemes give one mark for a conclusion. We checked the Evaluate parts from 2022 onward. 8 of the 24 with a mark scheme have a conclusion mark. All 8 are from November 2024 or later. That is 8 of the 9 mark schemes from that date on. End with a short overall judgement that brings your points together.

cites.quote: Valid conclusion drawing together/based on arguments presented in the answer (1)
Max one from: Conclusion: • One mark for a reasoned conclusion / overall judgement
One mark is available for a valid conclusion / judgement (must have considered both pros and cons).
Such discussions should end with a conclusion that revisits and brings together the points made.

points.text: If you leave out a conclusion, you can lose marks. In the March 2024 examiner report (Paper 12, Q9), examiners said students did not reach a realistic conclusion. This reduced their marks.

cites.quote: candidates largely failed to come to any realistic conclusion about encryption, which reduced the marks scored on the question.

points.text: Good answers take each point through three steps. First give a fact, then a consequence of that fact, then a judgement about how much it matters. Some mark schemes give a first mark for the point and more marks for the expansion. They also limit how many marks plain points can earn.

cites.quote: Good answers gave a description of how compression was used or of the effects of the compression and then added a consequence followed by a judgment as to the desirability or further effect of the compression.
Eight marks from: MAX four for 1st marks only Evaluations:
Must have expansions to be a proper evaluation

points.text: The most common mistake is describing how the thing works instead of judging it. Knowing the topic is not enough. You have to say whether each feature helps or causes problems.

cites.quote: Candidates seemed to have some understanding of each process, but preferred to describe each of these than actually evaluate their efficacy.
In some cases, candidates described how control technologies worked. Typically, this involved an in-depth discussion of sensors.
candidates were expected to make factual statements about project management software (PMS) and then expand on these with comments about whether these facts helped or hindered the project.

points.text: One-sided answers lose marks. Both sides must be there, but they do not need to be exactly equal. The examiners accepted more points for than against.

cites.quote: some candidates seemed not to understand the importance of ‘evaluate’ as a command word, and so gave a one-sided answer.
Candidates tended to concentrate on the positive implications, rather than both the positive and the negative, and this did restrict the overall marks scored for this question in a few cases.
Typically, candidates gave more answers in support than against, but this was acceptable.

points.text: Write in full sentences and paragraphs, not bullet points or a table. 9 of the 24 Evaluate mark schemes from 2022 on (all 2022-2024) cap a bulleted list. The cap is usually 6 of 8 marks (5 of 6 on 6-mark questions).

cites.quote: A detailed answer is needed, which cannot be achieved by writing bullet points.
Must be a proper evaluation for full marks. Max 6 marks if bullets/list of points.
Max. five marks if all three methods not covered Max. five marks if bullets/list of points
Answers with bulleted, short statements for free response questions, especially those requiring analyses, discussions and evaluations do not adequately answer the question.

points.text: Judge the thing in the scenario in the question, not in general. Some answers about spreadsheets never mentioned financial modelling, and they did badly.

cites.quote: To gain full credit, candidates must produce a reasoned evaluation that weighs up the advantages and disadvantages for the given scenario/context.
Whilst some lenience was allowed, candidates who failed to make any mention of financial modelling struggled to score well on this question.

points.text: Evaluate only what the question names. You do not need to compare it with other methods unless the question asks you to.

cites.quote: It was not necessary to compare pilot with other possible methods of implementation because the question asked candidates to ‘evaluate pilot implementation’ and made no mention of the other methods.

points.text: Evaluate is not the same as Discuss. Discuss asks you to write in depth in a structured way. Evaluate asks you to judge importance or value. You can give a judgement on each point or on the whole answer. We checked the 77 Discuss mark schemes from 2022 onward. None has a conclusion mark, but recent Evaluate mark schemes do.

cites.quote: Discuss write about issue(s) or topic(s) in depth in a structured way Evaluate judge or calculate the quality, importance, amount, or value of something
The command word ‘evaluate’ requires a judgement of the importance of the points being made about the method of prototyping.
In questions where an evaluation is, or evaluations are, required, the judgement can be for individual points or for an overall judgement on the whole content of the answer.

points.text: Some mark schemes give one mark for a short definition or description of the thing you evaluate. Keep it to one sentence, then start judging it.

cites.quote: One mark for a description of encryption (e.g. data scrambled/converted to cyphertext)
Valid definition / description of video-conferencing in education

question.quote: A person uses a dialogue interface to control multiple devices in their home. Evaluate the use of a dialogue interface in this context.

examples.context: You control a dialogue interface by speaking to it.

strong.sentence: Because the person controls the devices by speaking, they do not need to physically touch any switch or screen.

earns.quote: No need to physically interact (may exemplify) (1st)

strong.sentence: This is a real benefit for a disabled person, who can switch on lights or heating around the home without moving to them.

earns.quote: More accessible to disabled users (may refer to device itself or devices around the home) (1)

strong.sentence: It also means the person can carry on with other tasks, such as cooking, while giving a command.

earns.quote: Can undertake other tasks at the same time (1)

strong.sentence: However, the interface relies on sound, so loud music or a television in the room may stop it understanding the command.

earns.quote: External noise may result in the dialogue interface not understanding the command (1)

strong.sentence: It may also mishear what the person says and operate the wrong device, so the person can rely on it less.

earns.quote: Dialogue interface may misinterpret what is said (1)

strong.sentence: Overall, a dialogue interface is very useful in a home, especially for someone with limited movement, if the rooms are quiet enough.

earns.quote: One mark for a valid conclusion (1)

weak.answer: Dialogue interfaces are good for disabled people. You control things with your voice. It is hands-free and easy to use.
weak.why: Every point is positive. No point has a consequence, and there is no conclusion. So the answer cannot reach most of the marks for drawbacks and for the judgement.

basis.quote: Candidates tended to concentrate on the positive implications, rather than both the positive and the negative, and this did restrict the overall marks scored for this question in a few cases.

examples.note: Three sentences for, two against and one conclusion. The conclusion mark is easy to get if you remember to write one.

question.quote: A company is developing a data input screen for entering customer details into a database. Evaluate the use of evolutionary prototyping for developing the data input screen.

strong.sentence: In evolutionary prototyping, the developers keep refining and rebuilding the data input screen until it is complete.

earns.quote: The system / screen is continually refined and rebuilt (when developed using evolutionary prototyping)

strong.sentence: The staff who will use the screen work with every version of it during development.

earns.quote: The user continuously engages with the system (1)

strong.sentence: As a result, the screen is more likely to have the customer fields the staff need, which matters most for a data input screen.

earns.quote: so the new system / screen is more likely to meet the user requirements (1)

strong.sentence: The developers can also change the screen at any iteration, for example if the company decides to record extra customer details.

earns.quote: Screen / product can be changed at any stage / iteration (1)

strong.sentence: On the other hand, the constant meetings between developers and users can be costly.

earns.quote: Continual need to consult / interact between developers / client / end-users can be costly (1)

strong.sentence: This raises the overall cost of development, which is a serious drawback when the company is building only one screen.

earns.quote: which raises overall cost of development (1)

strong.sentence: Developers may also find it hard to know when to stop tweaking the screen, so development may go on too long.

earns.quote: Developers may have difficulty knowing when it is necessary to stop ‘tweaking’ / developing the system (1)

strong.sentence: Overall, evolutionary prototyping suits this screen because user feedback matters most for data entry, if the company sets a clear end point to control cost.

earns.quote: One mark is available for a valid conclusion / judgement (must have considered both pros and cons).

weak.answer: Evolutionary prototyping involves the users. The screen can be changed. It can be expensive. It takes a long time.
weak.why: These are bare statements. No statement has a consequence or a judgement after it, and there is no conclusion.

basis.quote: Weaker answers confused the methods of prototyping, made statements with no consequences, expansion, or judgments.

examples.note: Both answers contain the same facts. The strong answer earns more because it follows each fact with what it leads to and how much it matters. It also ends with a judgement.

thin_evidence: Evaluate has plenty of evidence: 25 question parts from 2022 onward (114 in all years). Assess is in the syllabus list of command words. But no question part uses Assess as its command word. A search of all question paper pages found no question that starts with 'Assess'. There are no Assess mark schemes or examiner report comments. So this report gives no separate advice for Assess beyond its syllabus definition ('make an informed judgement'). The count of conclusion marks comes from a text search of the mark schemes for 'conclusion' or 'overall judgement'.
